check.reason: The target is UnitedHealth and the insurer star-rating system, not patients, and patients are framed as the ones who live with the actual quality. It doesn't mock the reporter, target a private individual, quote the article, or touch death, children or violence. The headline is accurate to the story (a lawsuit over downgraded ratings). 'Worth billions' is a general characterization, not an invented specific figure, and fits what Medicare Advantage star ratings are known to be worth in bonus payments. The tone is dry and deadpan, and the piece is genuinely satirical.

pick.title: UnitedHealth sues to reverse downgraded Medicare Advantage quality scores
pick.headline: UnitedHealth Sues Government Over Insufficiently Appreciated Excellence, Which Happens to Be Worth Billions
pick.take: Quality is apparently a deeply held conviction that becomes a measurement error when the score drops. Insurers have found the one outcome worth taking to federal court: the star rating. Patients, who live with the actual quality, were not asked to file a brief.
